lede: Stations read against the page images of their sources only; each names its source. More will follow with the modules.

stations.text: Williston, population 100 by the gazetteer's count, has one general store, a saw and grist mill and a vegetable crate factory. The nearest railroad, express and telegraph are at Archer, eleven miles off.
stations.quelle: Florida State Gazetteer and Business Directory 1886–7, p. 458.

stations.titel: About 350 men on the line from Archer
stations.text: A trade journal reports about 350 men at work on the railway from Archer to Dunnellon, to be operated by the Florida Central & Peninsular.
The Plant System gives up its own line through the phosphate district near Albion and agrees with the Florida Central & Peninsular on the common use of the spur south of Archer.

stations.titel: Leased convicts in the pits and camps
stations.text: The state's leased convicts are worked in the county: about 160 near Albion, Levy county, mining phosphate, and about fifteen sublet to Colonel H. L. Morris of Morriston for the manufacture of naval stores.
stations.quelle: Report of the Commissioner of Agriculture of the State of Florida, 1893–1894, p. 67.

stations.text: The act to incorporate the town is approved; the first election is set for the first Tuesday in July. In 1905 the legislature declares the incorporation lawful after the fact.
stations.quelle: Laws of Florida 1905, ch. 5550, p. 870, and ch. 5549, p. 869.

stations.text: The state's Railroad Commission lists two stations named Williston, one on each road, and the same freight from both: ten cents a crate of vegetables, sixteen a box of oranges. The charge onward to the northern markets is beyond its control.
stations.quelle: First Annual Report of the Railroad Commission of the State of Florida (1898), pp. 12–13, 43, 86, 94.

stations.text: A federal soil survey finds that “the principal money crop in the vicinity of Williston is cucumbers”; peanuts are grown to fatten hogs, and the orange groves were lost in 1895.
stations.quelle: Rice and Geib, Soil Survey of the Gainesville Area, Florida, in: Field Operations of the Bureau of Soils, 1904, p. 278.

stations.text: Wash Bradley is lynched at Bronson, the county seat. The NAACP's list of 1919 records the accusation against him as “murder”.
stations.quelle: NAACP, Thirty Years of Lynching in the United States, 1889–1918 (1919), p. 55.

stations.text: Williston is an incorporated town on the Seaboard Air Line and the Atlantic Coast Line, with a bank, two hotels, a crate factory and a weekly paper.
stations.quelle: R. L. Polk & Co.'s Florida Gazetteer and Business Directory 1907–1908, p. 452.

stations.text: Florida's hard-rock phosphate falls from 477,538 tons (1913) to 310,267 tons; almost every ton shipped goes abroad. The state's list of phosphate companies opens with the Acme Phosphate Co. of Morriston.
stations.quelle: Florida Geological Survey, Seventh Annual Report (1915), pp. 21–22.

stations.text: The Seaboard Air Line advertises Williston as the seat of “the greatest cucumber industry in the State of Florida”, shipped “by the trainload” to the northern and western markets, with a photograph of a solid trainload leaving the town.
stations.quelle: Seaboard Air Line Railway, Shippers Guide 1914, pp. 69–71.
